Intro.description: Bringing digital experiences to life through design and code – intuitive, aesthetic, and user-centered.

About.title: About Me
About.description: During my Bachelor's degree in Media Informatics at TH Nürnberg, I gained a strong foundation in computer science and digital media. After graduating, I wanted to further specialize in web development, which led me to pursue a Master's degree in Interactive Technologies with a focus on Mobile at FH St. Pölten. My main focus is on understanding user experience and translating it into user-centered designs.
About.hobbies: In my free time, I like to explore topics around sustainability and enjoy trying out new vegan recipes. I love spending time outdoors – whether it’s running, hiking in the mountains, cycling, or going on bikepacking trips to discover new places and countries. Last year, for example, I cycled from Roth to Budapest and also explored Denmark and Sweden. For me, it’s the perfect way to leave everyday life behind and dive into new adventures.

wegweiser.description: Travel booking app designed to support environmentally conscious decisions throughout the booking process.

project.title: The Project
text: As part of my master’s thesis, I explored how travel booking apps can be designed to encourage more sustainable decisions. The goal was to develop design approaches that motivate users to make more environmentally conscious decisions without worsening the user experience. To do this, I created an interactive prototype integrating various design interventions.
The project was part of the Interactive Technologies master's program at FH St. Pölten, in the Mobile specialization.

problem.title: The Problem
text: Global tourism is responsible for around 8.8% of worldwide greenhouse gas emissions – with an annual increase of 3.5% between 2009 and 2019. The largest share comes from transport and mobility (49–75%), followed by accommodation (around 21%). Together, these two areas account for the majority of tourism-related emissions.

Despite this significant climate impact, sustainable travel options are rarely made visible on mainstream booking platforms. Many travelers are interested in greener alternatives, but often lack clear information or intuitive access points.
This raises the question of how digital platforms can better support travelers – through a motivating yet voluntary decision-making environment.

research.title: The Research Focus
text: This work combines ecological sustainability in tourism with persuasive design. At its core was the question of how users can be nudged toward more sustainable decisions through digital strategies such as nudging and gamification.
Another focus was on the user experience: How can sustainability and positive usability be aligned? This led to the following research questions:
- What sustainability strategies are already being implemented on booking platforms?
- Which nudging strategies effectively promote sustainable decisions on booking platforms?
- How do the prototype’s design interventions affect users?

concept.title: Planning the Journey
text: The project began with an extensive literature review to establish a theoretical foundation on sustainable travel and relevant behavioral strategies like nudging and gamification. This was followed by an analysis of existing booking platforms to identify design opportunities for sustainability-focused interventions.

A qualitative preliminary study provided insights into real decision-making processes and served as a basis for developing the prototype. The prototype developed as a result depicts four realistic booking scenarios. For evaluation, both moderated think-aloud tests (n = 10) and an unmoderated online test (n = 100) were conducted. Their findings informed the final design of the prototype. Finally, the study derives specific design recommendations for sustainable travel booking platforms.

prototyping.title: The Prototyping
text: A prototyping approach was used to test and refine the design interventions. The prototype was created in Figma. Initially, a low-fidelity version focused on layout, content, and core interactions—without being influenced by visual design.

This was followed by a high-fidelity prototype that combined a consistent visual identity, realistic content, and a modular component structure. It includes four distinct booking scenarios to allow targeted evaluation of the applied design strategies.

interventions.title: The Design Interventions
text: Based on the research findings, four booking scenarios were developed – from onboarding to selecting transport, accommodation, and travel inspiration. Each step integrates design interventions aimed at encouraging sustainable decisions.

Examples include CO₂ comparisons for transportation, visual highlighting of sustainable accommodations based on defined criteria, a loyalty points system, realistic representations of flight time and total cost, as well as standardized sorting and recommendation features.

branding.title: The Branding
text: The visual identity is designed to provide orientation, build trust, and intuitively support sustainable choices. The logo combines a stylized leaf and path to symbolize sustainability and direction. The color scheme features dark petrol tones complemented by fresh mint accents.

Typography, imagery, and a purposeful use of color – such as emission indicators – support a coherent, modern appearance. My goal was to create an app that doesn’t feel like a niche eco-product, but rather like a contemporary booking platform with clear added value for environmentally conscious travelers.

onlineTests.title: The Unmoderated User Tests
text: To evaluate the prototype, an unmoderated online test with 100 participants was conducted. Using the platform Useberry, the booking scenarios were tested in realistic conditions and user decisions were tracked. The tool also enabled detailed analysis via heatmaps, user flows, and screen recordings. Since participants interacted anonymously with the clickable prototype, more authentic choices were possible.
Short in-between questions and the User Experience Questionnaire (UEQ) provided additional insights into the interventions’ impact and the overall user experience.

thinkAloud.title: The Think-Aloud Tests
text: To gain a deeper understanding of the user perspective, ten moderated think-aloud tests were conducted. During these sessions, participants verbalized their thoughts while navigating the prototype. This allowed insights into their decision-making and their intuitive interpretation of icons, labels, and design cues.
The qualitative data revealed which elements were perceived as helpful, intrusive, or unclear – providing valuable input for refining the prototype.

results.title: The Results
text: The user experience was consistently rated positively: All UEQ results in both test settings were clearly within the positive range. Most participants chose sustainable options—especially when these were competitively priced.

The results show that visually appealing and low-threshold design strategies can influence decision-making behavior in favor of sustainable alternatives without significantly impairing the user experience. These include, for example, comparative emissions information, reward systems or positive highlighting of sustainable options. Red highlights were perceived by some test subjects as judgmental and potentially too intrusive. In particular, approaches that link sustainability with personal benefits were perceived as beneficial.

challenges.title: The Challenges
text: One of the key challenges was to make sustainability visible without users feeling manipulated or patronized. Strongly judgmental elements – such as red warning labels – can trigger resistance and damage long-term trust. The goal was to nudge users toward better choices without pressure – because only platforms that users enjoy will have long-term impact.

During implementation, I gained hands-on experience with Figma, component-based design, global styles and variables, and building interactive prototypes with animations. I also became familiar with Useberry as a tool for test execution and analysis.

weidlich.description: Website for a retired notary to present his lectures, publications, and professional background.
weidlich.type: WordPress Development ✦︎ SEO ✦︎ Web Design ✦︎ Corporate Branding ✦︎ Customer Service

project.title: The Project
text: A website was developed for Dr. Dietmar Weidlich to professionally showcase his expertise even after retiring from active notary service. As a retired notary, Dr. Weidlich continues to be professionally active – offering notary representations, publishing legal texts, and speaking at events.

The website is not intended for acquiring new clients, but rather addresses event organizers interested in booking him as a speaker. The content was designed to be usable during his active service and easily adaptable for his retirement starting end of July 2025.

features.title: Key Features
text: The website is based on the WordPress content management system and includes five main sections (Introduction, Publications, Lectures, Notary Representation Services, Contact) providing a clear overview of Dr. Weidlich’s work and expertise.

It features a GDPR-compliant contact form with SMTP integration for reliable email communication. Performance was enhanced through caching, local hosting of Google Fonts, and responsive design across devices. SEO measures were also implemented. Hosting, domain setup, and a professional email address were included as part of the project.

branding.title: Branding
text: The visual identity was developed as part of the project and includes a minimalist logo, a cohesive color scheme, web design, and business cards. The business cards feature a QR code linking directly to the website, along with contact details.

The main colors – a deep teal and a lighter cyan-blue – convey professionalism and trust. Combined with soft round elements, the design appears modern and structured. Typography and layout contribute to a clean and reliable look.

photography.title: Photography
text: The image selection was developed in close collaboration with the client. We met at his former notary office and organized a photoshoot using professional lighting equipment.

Most of the images used on the website – including portraits and photographs of his published works – were created specifically for this project. This results in a personal and authentic visual impression.

customer.title: Client Collaboration
text: From the beginning, the project was marked by close collaboration. We met regularly to align the layout, content, and overall structure of the site.

I initially built a version that reflected his active role as a notary, with the ability to seamlessly transition the content upon retirement. This included changes like converting the 'Notary Services' section to 'Notary Representation Services' and including updates to the imprint and privacy policy.

learnings.title: Learnings
text: This project was especially shaped by the aspect of client collaboration. I learned how important it is to offer expert guidance while also respecting a client’s individual wishes—and how to bring both together in a strong final result.

It was also my first time working with WordPress as a traditional CMS. While I had previous experience with WordPress, that had only involved developing custom themes and plugins. Here, I built the entire website without any custom programming.

Additionally, I explored SEO for the first time, including structured data, OpenGraph tags, and sitemaps. The experience taught me how much organization, responsibility, and iteration it takes to implement a real-world project on your own.

bevry.description: Web app for cocktail enthusiasts to discover, share, rate and manage drinks.
bevry.type: Full-Stack Development ✦︎ Corporate Branding ✦︎ User Testing ✦︎ Agile Teamwork

project.title: The Project
text: Bevry is a cocktail app created as part of my master’s program together with four fellow students.
The goal of the web app is to offer cocktail enthusiasts a platform where they can discover new recipes, share their own creations, and find inspiration for their next party.

logo.title: Logo Design
text: We developed several logo ideas and refined them through multiple iterations until we arrived at a design that convinced us all. The final logo features a gradient reminiscent of a Tequila Sunrise: transitioning from a fruity Mimosa orange to a rich Cosmopolitan pink.
This warm, playful color palette conveys freshness and energy, while the soft, organic shapes symbolize lightness and the sparkling vibrancy of a fizzy drink.
Within the organic bubbles, the letters B and Y are subtly hidden – matching the name Bevry. The 'Y' also resembles a martini glass, reinforcing the connection to the world of drinks.

photography.title: Visual Language
text: For the visual language, we relied on authentic photos created together with a photographer from our program during a cocktail shoot. Each of us prepared two drinks, which were then professionally photographed.

The corresponding recipes were also uploaded to the app, resulting in a consistent interplay between design and content. The images immediately make you crave a Moscow Mule, Espresso Martini, or Tropical Punch!

website.title: Brand Website
text: The website was developed with a strong focus on user-friendliness and appealing design. We used modern web technologies such as React and Next.js to ensure a fast and responsive user interface.
The content was carefully structured and presented in engaging layouts to invite users to browse and explore.

branding.title: Branding
text: In the course 'Brand Identity & Corporate Design' we developed the corporate identity for Bevry. We worked with Adobe InDesign, Adobe Photoshop, and Figma.
I created the logo, business stationery (business cards, letterheads, envelopes), stickers, website designs, and mockups.
Take a look at the brand book!

wireframes.title: App Design
text: At the beginning, we analyzed comparable apps to identify relevant features, content, information architecture, and design approaches, which then formed the basis for our own app strategy.
As a next step, we created low-fidelity wireframes to plan the basic structure and user flow of the app.
These wireframes were later refined into high-fidelity wireframes, which served as the foundation for the final app design.

backend.title: Technologies
text: For the backend, we used NestJS as a framework to ensure a clean architecture and modular structure. With TypeORM, we were able to manage our database entities efficiently and create a stable foundation for the application.

Authentication was implemented with JWT, while bcrypt ensured secure password encryption. We also used OpenAPI for automated endpoint documentation in Swagger, which greatly facilitated coordination between frontend and backend development.
On the frontend, we chose Vue.js as the framework, complemented by Vuetify, whose UI components helped us design a consistent user interface. For state management, we used Pinia.

testing.title: User Testing
text: After about two and a half months, we conducted our first usability tests. At that point, the core functionalities were already implemented, but the final design had not yet been defined.

The tests showed that most participants had a positive experience when searching for and posting cocktail recipes. Particularly praised were the clear categories, the large selection, and the modern, appealing design. At the same time, concrete areas for improvement were identified.

The evaluation was complemented by the Net Promoter Score (NPS), which, with a score of 60, indicates high user satisfaction and willingness to recommend. The results served as an important basis for targeted improvements in the second semester.

features.title: Features
text: From the very beginning, creating, editing, deleting, and sharing cocktail recipes was at the core. Registered users can browse the recipe collection, filter by category or ingredient, and save recipes in a favorites list. A rating and comment function allows for feedback and exchange. Step-by-step instructions make it easier to follow recipes.

With the Bar Inventory, users can keep track of their ingredients, while the Shopping List adds missing items directly from recipes. Users can also create custom ingredients and substitutes, save recipes as drafts, and receive personalized recommendations based on their bar inventory. Additionally, we integrated email verification, extended profile settings, and a loading animation.

games.title: Minigames
text: To make Bevry even more interactive and fun, we integrated a Games Hub featuring two minigames. The goal was to expand the joy of mixing cocktails both in groups and alone in a playful way.

‘Spin The Wheel’ is a party game focused on speed, chance, and group dynamics. Players take turns spinning a wheel that selects ingredients from their own bar inventory. When the hidden timer runs out, the last player must drink the resulting mix.

The second game, ‘Mix It Up,’ is designed for single players. Here, the goal is to collect the correct ingredients for a cocktail recipe while avoiding the wrong ones. Based on real recipes from Bevry, players can discover new drinks, earn bonus points, and compete on the high score board.

team.title: Agile Teamwork
text: The team consisted of five master’s students from FH St. Pölten: Laura, Sara, Sophia, Vani, and myself.

We worked with Scrum to organize ourselves. Sprint planning and reviews were held every two weeks during our weekly meetings. We used Jira to create tickets and track their status on the Kanban board.
We also collaborated with four fellow students from other master’s programs, including:
‘Photography’ for cocktail, marketing, and portfolio photos
‘Graphic Design’ for app design and icons
‘Sound Design’ for soundtracks and sound effects for the minigames
‘Animation’ for a loading animation and in-game animations for the minigames

myTasks.title: My Responsibilities
text: In addition to corporate branding, I was mainly responsible for backend development within the project. Among other things, I extended the user management, integrated email verification, and implemented the database logic for recipes, ingredients, substitutes, bar inventory, and shopping list.
I was also involved in frontend development with Vue.js. I supported the implementation of the new screen designs and integrated both the custom-designed icons and the loading animation.

learnings.title: Learnings
text: For me, the project was a valuable opportunity to go beyond my previous focus and learn new technologies. Working with NestJS in the backend was particularly challenging at first, as I had previously only basic knowledge of PHP and SQL.

I learned how important it is to carefully plan interfaces early on to ensure smooth collaboration between frontend and backend development. Overall, this gave me much more confidence in working with backend technologies, and I would definitely use NestJS again in future projects.

I also learned a lot about team organization and project planning. The two-week sprint cycles ensured continuous progress. At the same time, I realized that deployment and testing should not be left too late, as unexpected issues often arise here.

erika.description: App as a digital companion for climate-friendly actions and regional activities.
erika.type: Sustainable Web & App Design ✦︎ Prototyping ✦︎ Research

project.title: The Project
text: In the second semester of my master's program, I had the opportunity to work on a research project affiliated with the program's research institute. I chose the ERIKA project. The goal of the project is to develop the ERIKA app, which serves as a digital companion for climate-conscious actions in everyday life.

The app aims to promote climate-friendly behavior and highlight regional activities in the Waidhofen a/d Ybbs area. The focus is not only on sustainable content but also on sustainable aspects in the development and design of the app, ensuring a holistic implementation of the concept of sustainability.

implementation.title: The Implementation
text: During my work on the ERIKA research project, I conducted extensive research on the factors crucial for developing a sustainable website.

Additionally, I participated in researching and formulating research questions related to climate-friendly actions in daily life, the impacts of various measures, the role of digitalization, and the application of gamification to support sustainable behavior.
I analyzed and processed survey results and created a clickable prototype of the app.

sustainability.title: Sustainable Web & App Design
text: Sustainability is crucial in many aspects of life, yet we rarely consider how much the internet impacts our planet. Its CO₂ emissions are equivalent to those of aviation, accounting for about 2% of global emissions.
While researching sustainable web, app, and email design, I discovered various key factors, including hosting, efficient code, optimized images, thoughtful design, and the choice of colors and fonts.

Sustainable web design is not only environmentally beneficial but also enhances user experience, search engine rankings, and accessibility. Websites that consume fewer resources load faster, improving performance, user satisfaction, and overall reach.

prototyping.title: Prototyping
text: I created a Figma prototype for a user story of the ERIKA service. This interactive mockup demonstrates how the service informs users about sustainable initiatives.

The prototype includes a form for submitting initiatives, which appear in the calendar and map view after review. This allows users not only to participate in events but also to contribute their own ideas, increasing their ecological handprint.

The calendar and map views display upcoming initiatives and events. Each event has a detailed page with descriptions, dates, and location info. With GPS enabled, users receive notifications when near an event.

learnings.title: Learnings
text: The project gave me the opportunity to contribute to a research project at the university for the first time, providing insight into the processes from conceptualization and research to surveys and workshops. It was particularly exciting for me to be involved so early in the project and see how much conceptual work goes into the initial phases.
I found the content-related research especially enriching, particularly on the topics of behavior influence in digital applications, which later led me to dedicate my master's thesis to this subject.

Through the intensive engagement with sustainable web design, I also discovered many new aspects I hadn’t considered before and was able to apply parts of this knowledge directly to my own web development projects.

timeParabox.description: Interactive puzzle game with escape-box elements and a time travel theme, controlled by a native app.
timeParabox.type: App Development ✦︎ Hardware Integration ✦︎ Agile Teamwork

project.title: The Project
text: Time Parabox is an interactive escape box game that takes players on an exciting time-travel journey to repair paradoxes in history.
The adventure leads through five historical eras – Antiquity, the Middle Ages, the Renaissance, the Industrial Revolution, and World War II.

The project was carried out within the Master’s program 'Mobile' by a team of ten students. Development followed agile methods, with two-week sprints organized via Jira and weekly meetings to track progress.

concept.title: The Concept
text: Each era is represented by a physical puzzle box that incorporates NFC tags, magnetic locks, 3D-printed models, a rotary encoder, servomotors, and an LED ring.

An accompanying mobile app guides players through the puzzles and connects the physical components with digital interactions. Every puzzle is tailored to the historical era it represents. The ultimate goal is to stabilize the timeline and save the future.

story.title: The Storyline
text: In a future where time has fallen apart, your future self sends a mysterious box through a portal straight to you. Hidden inside are clues about a distorted past: great moments of history have been altered – the steam engine was never invented, Odysseus never returned home. Only you can set time back on track.

Guided by messages from your future self, you travel through eras, solve puzzles, and collect artifacts to restore the timeline. But in the end, the greatest revelation awaits: the mysterious person who sent you on this journey… is you.

app.title: The App
text: Before development began, low-fidelity wireframes were created to define the structure, navigation, and user flows of the app. These early sketches helped align the puzzle mechanics with the digital interface.
Next, the lo-fi drafts were refined into high-fidelity wireframes. These hi-fi screens formed the foundation for implementation and ensured a smooth handover between design and development.

The app was developed with React Native, using React Redux for state management and Expo for setup and testing. Native smartphone sensors such as the accelerometer and microphone were integrated to enable specific puzzle interactions.

architecture.title: The System Architecture
text: Communication between the app and the puzzle boxes is managed by an ESP32 microcontroller, which acts as the central hub. Using Bluetooth Low Energy (BLE), it exchanges data between the app and the electronic components inside the boxes.
This made it possible to directly synchronize interactions such as scanning artifacts, unlocking boxes, controlling the LED ring, or triggering sensors with the digital game state.

box.title: The Box Design
text: At the heart of the project is a main box that contains several smaller puzzle boxes. These incorporate a variety of electronic and mechanical components, including NFC tags, magnetic locks, 3D-printed models, a rotary encoder, servomotors, and an LED ring.

To bring each era to life, we designed and produced 3D-printed artifacts, each embedded with an NFC chip. Players received these artifacts as rewards for solving puzzles and needed them at the end to unlock the final box. The objects were printed in the university’s Makers’ Lab, hand-painted, and integrated into the game.

myTasks.title: My Tasks
text: My main responsibility was developing the app with React Native. Beyond general app development, I implemented specific puzzle mechanics.

In Antiquity, I developed the integration of a digital compass that helped players guide Odysseus on his journey. For the Renaissance, I implemented accelerometer-based controls that allowed players to dodge obstacles with Leonardo da Vinci’s flying machine. In the World War II section, I co-designed a puzzle where players had to decode Morse messages to obtain the final artifact.

presentation.title: The Presentation
text: Together with a fellow student, I organized the presentation of Time Parabox at the FH St. Pölten project exhibition. We designed the exhibition stand as well as a slideshow, postcards, stickers, flyers, and posters. We also created the logo and a consistent corporate design.

Additionally, we developed a social media concept for LinkedIn and Instagram to increase the project’s visibility. Our goal was to create a cohesive and engaging presentation that sparked curiosity and encouraged visitors to try out the game.

learnings.title: Learnings
text: In this project, I was able to gain valuable new experiences. For the first time, I worked with React Native and Expo, which gave me a solid introduction to native app development. I also found it particularly exciting to work with smartphone sensors that we integrated into the puzzle mechanics.

In addition, collaborating in a large team of ten people was a very instructive experience. At first, I was concerned that organizing such a big group might be challenging. However, by using Scrum, running regular sprints, and defining clear responsibilities within smaller subgroups, team coordination worked smoothly and efficiently.

Although my focus was mainly on the app and I worked less directly with the hardware, I found it fascinating to see how the various hardware and software components interlock and communicate with each other.

pgmon.description: Community app for sharing Pokémon sightings with map view and playful UI elements.

project.title: The Project
text: As part of my first Master’s semester, I developed a web application together with two fellow students in the courses Advanced Web Programming and Business Application Development. The project, called PGMon+ (Pokémon GO Monitor Add), serves as a playful extension to the popular Pokémon GO app.

The goal was to allow players to share Pokémon sightings via an interactive map, making it easier for others to find them. While some core features were predefined, we had creative freedom to extend the functionality on both the frontend and backend.

features.title: Features
text: The application enables users to log Pokémon sightings on a map and view the findings of other players nearby. A registered account is required for submitting entries, while the overview map remains accessible to everyone.
In addition, the app includes user management as well as light and dark mode. By combining Material Design Lite with custom components, we created a modern and intuitive interface.

implementation.title: Technical Implementation
text: The frontend was developed with Vue.js and built using Vite. Pinia was used for global state management.
The backend is based on Spring Boot and provides a REST API that handles all user, login, and sighting data. Communication between frontend and backend is managed via Axios.
Furthermore, Maven was used as the build tool and JUnit for automated testing.

role.title: My Role in the Project
text: In addition to implementing several backend endpoints, I was mainly responsible for integrating Google Maps, implementing snackbar notifications and input validations, as well as developing custom input components. I also ensured a fully responsive design throughout the application.

Creative additions such as an animated 'PokeSpinner' loading indicator or playful feedback in the registration form – featuring the Pokémon 'Diglett' emerging from the ground upon correct password input – added unique character to the app. These features made the application not only functional, but also engaging and highly user-friendly.

learnings.title: Learnings
text: Through this project I was able to deepen my knowledge of Vue.js and gain a stronger understanding of how frontend and backend interact. Working with external APIs such as Google Maps and the PokéAPI was also an exciting experience.

On top of that, I gained valuable practical experience in team collaboration and version control with Git. Overall, the project was a rewarding combination of technical learning and creative implementation.

Disclaimer: All Pokémon shown in this project belong to their respective rights holders (Nintendo, Game Freak, Creatures) and are used here solely for demonstration purposes as part of a study project.

museumverse.description: Audio guide app that uses AI to create personalized and dynamically generated museum experiences.

project.title: The Project
text: As part of the master’s course in Business Planning, I worked with four fellow students to develop a complete business plan. The goal was to design an innovative business idea and demonstrate its feasibility through a proof of concept.
Our idea was an audio guide app that uses artificial intelligence to enable personalized and dynamically generated museum experiences. With our app MuseumVerse, museums can be experienced digitally.

idea.title: The Idea
text: The key feature of the app is hyper-personalization, ensuring that every museum visitor receives tailored audio guide content in real time, which continuously adapts to visitor behavior throughout the museum tour.

The onboarding begins with a short interactive questionnaire that captures interests, goals, and demographic data to create a visitor profile. Based on this, a personalized audio guide and a matching tour are generated – making each museum visit a unique experience.

Another feature is interactivity, enabled through a chat function. Visitors can engage in playful and informative dialogues not only with the narrator of the guide, but also with artists or even with the exhibits themselves.

poc.title: The Proof of Concept
text: During the project, we had regular mentoring sessions where we received feedback on our business idea and refined our strategy. In addition, we pitched our idea several times in front of a jury – a valuable exercise in presenting complex content concisely and responding convincingly to critical questions.

To make the idea tangible, a teammate and I developed an interactive Figma prototype. It showcases the onboarding with questionnaire, the generation of individual tours, the chat function, and the personalized presentation of exhibits including additional information.

learnings.title: Learnings
text: Through this project, I gained insights into creating business plans and, for the first time, approached a product from a business perspective. This included considering how it could become financially profitable, which business models might apply, and which subplans (e.g., personnel, finance, sales planning, as well as profit and loss statement) make up a complete business plan.
The project showed me the importance of thinking about technical feasibility, user experience, and economic viability together.

veganAdvent.description: Digital advent calendar with valuable tips and information for a vegan lifestyle.

background.title: The Project Background
text: This so-called Print2Mobile project was carried out as part of the Master's degree program Interactive Technologies at FH St. Pölten. The goal was to seamlessly guide users from a physical medium into the digital world with the help of a QR code.

Particularly important here is compliance with certain design and usability rules to ensure that the transition is clear, accessible, and suitable for all devices. My approach was to implement this concept in the form of a digital advent calendar.

project.title: The Project
text: The idea behind the Advent calendar was to provide a daily tip or piece of information about veganism from December 1st to 24th. Unlike traditional advent calendars, I deliberately chose not to restrict access to individual days. This way, the content remains available at all times in line with the course requirements, since users can access all content regardless of the date.
The goal of the project was not only to share recipes, but also to raise awareness of the benefits of a vegan lifestyle and to provide easy-to-understand information.

poster.title: The Poster
text: The centerpiece of the Print2Mobile project is a poster showing 24 numbered QR codes. By scanning one of the codes, users are taken directly to the corresponding door in the digital advent calendar.
As an alternative to the poster, the codes can also be cut out and individually integrated into a physical advent calendar.

implementation.title: Implementation
text: The web application was developed with React and Tailwind CSS. For door 2, I integrated an interactive chart using ApexCharts.

In addition, the app offers a Light/Dark/System mode that adapts to the operating system settings and is stored in Local Storage. Not only background and text colors, but also the SVG graphic on the homepage dynamically adjust to the selected mode.
Further information about the project and the source code can be found on GitHub.

challenges.title: Learnings
text: What was particularly exciting was that I worked with Tailwind CSS for the first time in this project. Getting started was surprisingly easy, and I really enjoyed working with variables, especially for Dark and Light mode. Implementing the theme switcher was also a new experience that turned out to be straightforward yet instructive.

Another challenge was to follow the '10 rules for QR codes'. In addition, generating 24 individual QR codes for the poster was time-consuming. Nevertheless, I was convinced by the idea, as it provides a direct and playful access to the web app.

ecocalypse.description: Immersive video game scene focusing on worldbuilding and visual storytelling.

project.title: The Project
text: In my second master's semester, I participated in a one-week Summer School workshop. I chose Environmental Storytelling, which focused on worldbuilding as well as environmental and visual storytelling.

The project involved creating a static or interactive immersive video game scene using Unity and pre-made assets. The scene needed to be realistic, visually engaging, and functional for a game environment, with a strong emphasis on applying the principles of environmental storytelling.

In a small team of four, we developed the game concept Ecocalypse, a game set in the year 2035 after a climate catastrophe. A year earlier, the entire rainforest had burned down, triggering climate collapse and the breakdown of the global order.

scene.title: The Scene
text: The scene is set in a room of an elegant house that was once Joseph’s office. After the unexpected collapse of infrastructure, he barricaded himself there, waiting for the right time to escape to the countryside to reunite with his family.

The player discovers traces of his daily life and preparations for escape, including personal belongings, notes, and supplies. The room is ransacked and bears the marks of a violent raid in which Joseph was killed for his resources. Now, the intruders are using his supplies, while the room paints a vivid picture of Joseph’s desperate struggle for survival and his tragic demise.

objects.title: The Objects
text: Carefully placed objects narrate the game's story and provide background context. Newspaper articles on the walls report on the crisis. A family portrait hints at a rural safe haven. A city map highlights Joseph’s planned escape route.

A wall calendar marks January 2035, showing Joseph’s attempts to keep track of time. His detailed daily routine reflects his struggle against isolation. An unfinished letter to Julia reveals his thoughts and emotions. An ad for H2-NO underscores extreme water scarcity and the world's dire conditions.
These elements create an immersive scene that effectively applies the principles of environmental storytelling.

implementation.title: The Implementation
text: My responsibilities in the project were diverse and included aspects of worldbuilding, storytelling and the creation of in-game objects, such as newspaper articles. Additionally, I was responsible for selecting the necessary low-poly assets for Unity.

When creating the storyline, we paid special attention to integrating behavioral traces, identity claims, and mood modifiers. These elements had to be cohesive to create an immersive experience. Any inconsistencies in the room, lighting, or sound could break the players’ immersion and disrupt the experience.

learnings.title: Learnings
text: Before the Summer School, I was hardly familiar with the concept of environmental storytelling. Through the project, however, I was able to immerse myself in the world of game design and gain hands-on experience with worldbuilding, environmental, and visual storytelling. What I found especially exciting was not just telling a story, but making it tangible through space, objects, and atmosphere. The key was to create a coherent and immersive world where every detail contributes to the overall narrative.

I also gained my first experience working with Unity, a tool I had barely encountered before. What I found particularly valuable was the collaboration within our interdisciplinary team: by assigning tasks based on our strengths, we were able to leverage different skill sets effectively—ensuring that not everyone needed to be a Unity expert to achieve a compelling result.

trilum.description: Analysis and redesign of the user interface for the wireless Pick-by-Light system TRILUM to enhance usability.
trilum.type: Web Development ✦︎ Web Design ✦︎ Human-Centered Design ✦︎ Usability Testing

project.title: The Project
text: As part of my bachelor's thesis, I analyzed and redesigned the graphical user interface of the Pick-by-Light system TRILUM. The system, developed by the Fraunhofer Society at the Fraunhofer Institute for Integrated Circuits (IIS), served as the foundation for my work.

In collaboration with Fraunhofer IIS, where I was hired as a student assistant in the Supply Chain Services group in Nuremberg following my mandatory internship, I had the opportunity to write my bachelor's thesis. My goal was to improve the usability of the web application.
Access to my bachelor's thesis is password-protected — just reach out to me for the login details

init.title: Starting Point
text: TRILUM is a wireless Pick-by-Light system for warehouse picking and assembly processes. The system guides employees who need to retrieve materials from shelves to the correct compartment using light signals.
However, the focus of my work was on the desktop application developed using the Angular framework. This application is used to coordinate orders, manage inventory, and oversee employees.

implementation.title: Implementation
text: To emphasize user-centricity, the user-centered design process according to ISO standard 9241/210 was applied.
First, the application was analyzed. During this phase, other Pick-by-Light systems were reviewed, and user requirements were documented.

To design and conduct usability tests, appropriate usability evaluation methods were selected. Users were surveyed using a questionnaire, and the think-aloud method was employed to observe user behavior.

Based on the test evaluations, usability issues were identified, and design solutions were developed to improve the user experience. The optimization proposals were then prioritized and implemented in the existing system, followed by a second round of usability testing.

result.title: The Result
text: The results of the follow-up tests show that the system's usability was significantly improved, allowing for more intuitive interaction. Participants not only found the tasks easier to complete but also rated the interaction principles much higher.

nakt.description: WordPress website without pre-built themes or plugins. The focus was on PHP programming.

project.title: The Project
text: NAKT? Interested? NAKT is the name of a WordPress website that I developed together with three classmates as part of a study project in the sixth semester. The name is derived from the first letters of our first names.

What makes this website special is that no pre-built themes, plugins, shortcodes, etc., were used, as these had to be programmed independently. The focus was on PHP development, although HTML, JavaScript, and CSS were also utilized. I also made sure that the content could be displayed in both German and English by implementing localization.

implementation.title: The Implementation
text: For the project, I developed a 'Recipes' plugin, allowing the user to create their own recipes. I also programmed a widget with various configuration options, which displays posts randomly. The user can also submit sustainability tips, for which I developed a JSON export.
Further information about the project and the commented source code of my implemented components can be found on GitHub.
